findings.title: effect resolution accepts a foreign lease and has no row-scope binding
findings.recommendation: At EffectReconciler#resolve validate the lease inside the transaction as #reconcile already does, require the loaded row's thread_id/namespace to equal the lease's, and include both columns in the conditional UPDATE, raising CheckpointConflictError before appending a transition. Add a shared-adapter A/B test.
findings.reproduction: Shared-adapter probe: thread.b writer holding a valid thread.b lease resolved a thread.a unsafe effect to succeeded; returned record still reports thread_id=thread.a.
findings.new_supporting_fact: resolve is the only effect mutation path with neither a lease check nor an attempt-token check; prepare, start, reconcile and complete each have one of the two.

findings.title: the eight-row claim window makes a valid queued resume unreachable
findings.recommendation: In claim_request_in_transaction, when every row in the window was deferred as an early turn, add the oldest eligible :resume for the open occurrence beyond the window and run it through the same validator and fence. Merely raising 8 relocates the hole. Add a regression with 8 early turns plus a valid resume.
findings.reproduction: Probe at 582ae55: early_turns=7 -> run_next=resume; early_turns=8/9/12 -> run_next=nil on three consecutive attempts, with resume.1 left status=queued at enqueue_sequence=9.
findings.boundary_correction: Starvation begins at 8 deferred turns, not 9 as recorded in analyses/request-claim-starvation.md; with exactly 8 the LIMIT 8 window is full.

findings.title: a schedule's canonical digest is accepted unverified and survives the SQLite round-trip
findings.root_cause: The shared Schedule value object treats a supplied definition_digest as authority rather than as a claim to verify; this gem then faithfully persists and re-reads it without recomputation, so the false provenance becomes durable.
findings.recommendation: Mirror Capability::Descriptor: compute the canonical digest after validate!, require exact equality when a digest is supplied, and freeze the retained value. Add a SQLite round-trip test proving a forged row cannot materialize.
findings.reproduction: Override accepted while differing from canonical and not frozen; after put_schedule the stored digest reads back as the forged sha256:000...0.

findings.title: three comms/inbox read paths are unbounded
findings.root_cause: The shared REQUEST_SELECT history helper and two comms status helpers were written for the reading caller's convenience; the bounding convention applied to the sibling projections in the same files was not applied to them.
findings.recommendation: Apply the convention already present in these files: give request_history a limit: via the existing history_limit bound, and add LIMIT to the two comms status helpers.
